title: How Engineering Managers Can Turn Team Growth Into Visible Impact
author: Gregoro Jalstersek
summary: Guest author Alex Ponomarev presents a framework for engineering managers to track and communicate the growth of their teams as a core measure of leadership impact. Rather than viewing success through shipped features alone, he argues managers should measure team development through signals like time to independence, performance review trajectory, coaching cadence, and scope expansion. The piece provides practical tools for turning invisible people work into visible organizational value through lightweight artifacts and stakeholder-ready communication.
points: Manager impact is measured through people growth, not just feature delivery.
Track growth signals: independence timelines, trajectory, feedback cadence, scope expansion, and retention with momentum.
Translate growth outcomes into stakeholder language (capacity, cost, delivery) not just learning language.
Avoid the trap of retention without momentum—people staying without visible progression is a false positive.
Build visible proof through growth maps, stability notes, and before/after stories.
quotes: Features fade, they get replaced, rewritten, or retired. But the growth of the people you manage is your lasting legacy.
Your job is to make those conditions real, then protect them. That's how I think about talent development.
The deeper win is watching someone who needed handholding a year ago start coaching others.
Treat 'people problems' like product problems: isolate, experiment, fix, repeat.
Growing your people is delivering results, and showing that growth is how you show your impact.” Archived from Engineering Leadership on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
